claims.claim: Intel identity/tradability is validated as NASDAQ INTC / Intel Corporation (CIK 0000050863); cumulative primary lineage contains issuer Q2 results and the Q2 2026 Form 10-Q, with duplicate URL/origin representations collapsed rather than treated as independent corroboration.

Q2 primary evidence is current enough for T0 operating underwriting; a current independent market source dated September 2026 supplies valuation context. Issuer and SEC versions share the same company-origin economics and are not counted as independent evidence of issuer claims.

risks.risk: Issuer and SEC earnings evidence are not independent corroboration of management claims; valuation evidence is independent but market-derived.

unknowns.unknown: No independent source establishes durable external-foundry economics; this remains a non-gating uncertainty reflected conservatively in score/confidence.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue was $16.128B and GAAP operating income $1.796B; DCAI revenue rose 59% YoY while Foundry remained structurally loss-making at a $2.089B operating loss on $5.765B revenue.

The $11.033B GAAP net loss was dominated by a separately disclosed $12.529B mark-to-market loss on Escrowed Shares, so the quarter supports operating improvement without implying Foundry profitability.
Current September 2026 market capitalization near $574B after a large share-price re-rating makes valuation demanding relative to still-unproven external-foundry economics.

risks.risk: Foundry remains deeply loss-making and external revenue is small; 18A/14A economics depend on yield, utilization and committed external demand.
A roughly $574B market capitalization embeds substantial turnaround expectations after a major 2026 re-rating.

contradictions.contradiction: Strong operating improvement coexists with weak Foundry economics; the prior headline GAAP-loss contradiction was resolved by primary-source reconciliation rather than ignored.

unknowns.unknown: Normalized external Foundry margins and durable external utilization remain unproven.
No current evidence supports exceptional pricing power for Intel Foundry.

thesisQuality.basis: Strong product/process relevance and renewed growth support a strong band, but external Foundry value capture remains unproven.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue and operating income improved materially, offset by large Foundry losses and capital intensity.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: September market capitalization near $574B after a sharp re-rating is demanding versus still-unproven Foundry returns.

catalystScore.basis: 18A-P risk production, 18A high-volume manufacturing and 14A/customer-demand milestones provide multiple identifiable catalysts, with execution uncertainty.

governancePower.basis: Disclosure is adequate and capital allocation is being directed toward leading-edge capacity, but current evidence does not establish exceptional stewardship or returns on that capital.

alignment2036.basis: AI/server compute and domestic leading-edge semiconductor capacity are foundational long-duration infrastructure exposures.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Products, data-center/AI and Foundry reuse process, manufacturing and packaging capabilities across multiple demand engines.

bottleneckControl.basis: Intel controls meaningful domestic leading-edge capacity and process capability, but TSMC and other foundries remain credible substitutes and external utilization is not established.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Multiple product and foundry paths provide optionality, while turnaround economics remain sensitive to node execution and external demand.

substitutionResilience.basis: Process roadmap and x86 ecosystem provide replacement barriers, but competing CPUs/accelerators and foundries remain material substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Domestic manufacturing footprint and internal manufacturing capability improve resilience, while leading-edge fab complexity and capital intensity remain dependencies.

pricingPower.basis: Current evidence does not demonstrate durable Foundry scarcity rent or external pricing power; large Foundry losses argue for conservative treatment.

riskEvidence.basis: Material execution, utilization, capital-intensity and valuation risks remain despite operating improvement; Foundry losses are still large.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Primary issuer/SEC evidence directly supports operating facts and an independent current market source supports valuation; external-foundry economics remain an explicit unknown.

scoreRecord.thesis: Intel combines improving compute demand with strategically important domestic leading-edge manufacturing; value creation depends on converting process milestones into durable product economics and materially better Foundry utilization/profitability.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: The market may be pricing a successful Foundry/18A turnaround before external utilization and normalized Foundry returns are demonstrated.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: 18A/18A-P production and yield progression plus evidence of committed external Foundry demand and improving segment economics.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore records the methodology-weighted 12-component evidence score; risk and confidence are separately source-addressed for canonical runtime treatment.
